findings.description: The CMK protecting the logs bucket omits enable_key_rotation, which defaults to false, so the key material is never automatically rotated and is used indefinitely. Long-lived key material widens the exposure window if the key is ever compromised and fails common key-management baselines for data at rest.

No policy argument is supplied, so AWS applies the default key policy delegating full control to the account root, meaning any IAM principal in the account granted kms permissions can use, disable, or schedule deletion of the key that protects log data. This removes the cryptographic separation-of-duties boundary that would otherwise protect audit records from tampering or unauthorised decryption.

deletion_window_in_days is set to the minimum of 7 days, giving only a brief window to cancel an accidental or malicious key deletion; destroying this CMK would render the encrypted log data permanently unrecoverable.
